keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 215,209 km2 (892 cells): Rostov, Pereslavl-Zalessky, Suzdal, Yuryev-Polsky, Yaroslavl, Kostroma, Galich, Uglich, Vologda, Dmitrov and Klin (a gazetteer test, not a page), but not Vladimir itself, the capital ('Capital: ... Vladimir (1157-1389)'), which sits in Cliopatria's Golden Horde shape. The page: 'By the end of the 13th century, the grand principality had fragmented into over a dozen appanages' and 'Alexander Nevsky (r. 1252-1263) was the last prince to reign directly in Vladimir', so the shape is the sum of the appanages round the old capital. The infobox gives no area, so the factor-of-two check cannot be made (the only size figures on the pages are Moscow's). The Yaroslavl lands (all of Yaroslavl Oblast, 99% in this shape) are inside it although the Yaroslavl page makes the Principality of Yaroslavl a separate state from 1218 to 1463 that 'separated from Vladimir-Suzdal'; they are kept because no Yaroslavl dossier exists yet and the Vladimir-Suzdal page counts Yaroslavl among the eleven appanages of the grand principality (see notes). OVERLAP WITH TVER (reconciled 2026-10-31): Cliopatria's shape of 1294 shares 28 cells (about 7,100 km2; 35.87-38.26E 56.30-57.71N): 20 on the Klin-Dmitrov edge (35.87-37.88E, 56.30-57.08N) and 8 on the Uglich-Kalyazin edge (37.84-38.26E, 57.16-57.71N) with the Tver correction of tver.json (gazetteer arithmetic, not a page). The Principality of Tver page lists a 'Principality of Klin, around the town of Klin' among Tver's appanages (mid-14th century, undated) and has Tver stretch 'from Kashin in the east to Zubtsov in the west'; the Vladimir-Suzdal page names neither Klin nor Kalyazin. Both dossiers cannot hold these cells, so the Tver reading wins and they are subtracted here; Cliopatria itself has them in Vladimir-Suzdal (Klin to 1304) and then in Moscow's shape.

wars.name: Struggle between Moscow and Tver for the grand princedom of Vladimir
wars.outcome: Moscow prevailed: Ivan I became sole grand prince in 1331, the throne was united with Moscow's for good by 1389, and Tver became Dmitry's junior ('elder brother') in 1375.

wars.name: Tver Uprising of 1327
wars.outcome: Tver's rising of 15 August 1327 was crushed by a Mongol force led by Ivan of Moscow and Alexander of Suzdal; in 1328 Ozbeg divided the grand principality between Alexander of Suzdal and Ivan I of Moscow, and on Alexander's death in 1331 Ivan was sole grand prince.

notes:
Page budget 5 (Vladimir-Suzdal, Principality of Rostov (a redirect to the same article), Principality of Yaroslavl, Principality of Moscow, Ivan III); the Tver Uprising page was opened for the Tver dossier and used for 1328. SAME STATE AS principality-of-rostov-suzdal (Wikidata Q83546; one Wikipedia article, 1125-1389): kept as two dossiers because the earlier row belongs to another batch (its dossier names this one as successor). Cliopatria has no shape for 1241-1293 (its Mongol Empire shape covers the land); the page has the state continuous ('Yaroslav II (r. 1238-1246) and the other princes submitted to Mongol rule'; Alexander Nevsky 1252-1263), so a merged dossier should carry a confidence-1 keyframe for 1241-1293. WHAT THE CLIOPATRIA ROW IS: the shapes are the lands of the old Rostov-Suzdal country that were not drawn as Moscow, Tver, Nizhny Novgorod or Beloozero, shrinking as each shape's lost cells (computed with the gazetteer) go to Cliopatria's Moscow shape: 113 cells in 1305, 18 in 1333, 264 in 1344, 37 in 1375, 91 in 1395, 29 in 1415, 184 in 1422, 133 in 1463, 15 in 1482. The row never contains Vladimir itself: the capital lies inside Cliopatria's Golden Horde or Blue Horde shape 1294-1400 (and inside Moscow's from about 1420), so every shape to 1389 is adjusted with a 70 km disc. The page ends the Grand Principality of Vladimir in 1389 (infobox; 'by 1389, the two thrones were permanently united') or 1394 ('since 1394, Moscow effectively inherited the title'); I end the dossier on 19 May 1389 (Dmitry Donskoy's death and will) and mark the shapes of 1395-1486 'wrong': they are the Rostov, Yaroslavl, Uglich, Bezhetsk and Vologda appanages, not a Vladimir state (Yaroslavl page: a separate principality 1218-1463; Ivan III page: Yaroslavl absorbed 1463, Rostov 1474, Andrey Bolshoy's appanage seized 1491-1493). These lands need dossiers (principality-of-yaroslavl, principality-of-rostov, principality-of-uglich proposed); until then they will be blank on the map after 1389. The Golden Horde dossier (ia-02) has vassal_start (1294) and vassal_end (1480) events for this slug; with a 1389 end the vassal_end of 1480 should be re-aimed at Moscow. Not settled: the Yaroslavl lands (153 cells in 1294) were already a separate principality by the Yaroslavl page though Cliopatria draws them as Vladimir-Suzdal; I kept them for lack of a Yaroslavl dossier (subtract the Yaroslavl' oblast cells when one exists); Suzdal was ruled by its own princes (Alexander of Suzdal 1327-1331, Konstantin 1355: Moscow page) and the Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod principality is another dossier; the 1328 division of the grand principality gives no lands. Area check: the infobox has no area; the Ivan III page gives Moscow 'less than 600 square miles (1,600 square kilometres)' under Ivan II and 'more than 15,000 square miles (39,000 square kilometres)' at the end of Vasily II's reign (1462), against Cliopatria's Moscow 10,246 km2 (1294) and 317,907 km2 (1453-1462): a factor of eight for the Moscow dossier. Gazetteer names: none needed (Vladimir, Rostov Veliky and Yaroslavl' resolve). REPAIR 2026-10-31 (reviewer findings of review-eu-16-g): (1) the 1389 merge now carries only the core that passes to Moscow (identity.successors[0] land: the 1375 shape without the 1395 shape, plus the Vladimir disc); the remaining land of the 1375/1395 shapes (364 cells after the Tver subtraction) is given by four loss events in May 1389: Yaroslavl (84 cells), Rostov (12), Uglich-Bezhetsk (19), all confidence 1, and the other 249 cells (150 of them in Vologda Oblast) to 'nobody' as a placeholder for a holder no page names; the sizes of the discs (Rostov 40 km, Uglich 40 km, Bezhetsk 40 km) are mine and the Yaroslavl cells are what remains of Yaroslavl Oblast. Counterpart dossiers principality-of-yaroslavl, principality-of-rostov, principality-of-uglich are proposed, not written. Note that the Ivan III page makes Uglich, Bezhetsk and Vologda appanages of Vasily II's sons (Moscow's own dynasty) by 1462, so a Moscow dossier may prefer to carry them as Moscow land from Cliopatria's dates (Bezhetsk 1415, Vologda country 1422, Uglich 1482). (2) vassal_start 1294 and vassal_end May 1389 with counterpart golden-horde added (the page gives the vassalage without a year). (3) Overlap with the Tver dossier: the Tver correction (Tver 75 km + Kashin 45 km + Zubtsov 45 km) is subtracted from every keyframe of 1294-1389 (28 cells in 1294, 8 in 1305-1332, 7 from 1333); the Tver page lists Klin among Tver's appanages and the Vladimir-Suzdal page does not name Klin or Kalyazin; Klin's owner is stated in /ledger/2. (4) The 'wrong' keyframes of 1395-1486 now say in their correction text that they are not to be drawn for this slug. THIN ITEMS RE-TRIED 2026-10-31: the Ivan I of Moscow page (acquisitions) and the Dmitry Donskoy page (Galich, will) give no year for any of Moscow's acquisitions from this row (1305 Pereslavl/Dmitrov/Klin, 1333 Mologa, 1344 Galich/Kostroma/Vologda, 1375 Yuryev-Polsky), so those four loss events stay at confidence 1; Ivan I page: 'Ivan controlled Novgorod and Kostroma' after the 1328 division. The Grand Prince of Vladimir page supplied a ruler table (13 reigns 1293-1389), now in identity.rulers. The Grand Prince page does not call Vladimir a vassal; the vassalage sentences are on the Vladimir-Suzdal page.
